visa = an official permission, often a stamp or document, to enter a country
transit visa = permission to pass through a country on the way to another destination
e-visa = a visa you apply for and receive online rather than in a passport sticker
biometric passport = a passport with a chip storing a photograph and other identity data
customs declaration = a form stating what goods you are bringing into a country
confiscate = to officially take something away, for example at security or customs
insurance claim = a formal request for an insurer to pay for a loss
excess = the first amount of a loss that you pay yourself under an insurance policy
flight compensation = money an airline may owe you after a long delay or cancellation
diverted = sent to a different airport than the one on the ticket
stranded = unable to continue a journey, often because of cancelled transport
tourist scam = a trick designed to take money from visitors who do not know local prices or rules
unlicensed taxi = a private car that offers rides without official permission
seasickness = feeling ill because of the movement of a boat
airsickness = feeling ill because of the movement of a plane
foreign currency = the money used in another country
bureau de change = an office that exchanges one currency for another
traveller's cheques = paper cheques bought in advance that can be cashed abroad
prepaid card = a card you load with money before you travel, then spend abroad
travel adapter = a plug that lets you use electrical devices in another country's sockets
